---
title: "Library-level calibration of the TSS cap signature"
output: github_document
---

A read whose 5' end is a capped RNA end carries one more untemplated G than the library's
uncapped reads (reverse transcriptase adds a C opposite the cap; `../cap_signature_other_datasets/`).
LRAA v0.46.0 used that signature to prune TSSs that look like 5' truncation products, but
decided *per splice graph* whether a library showed the signature at all. In the genome-wide
FTD run that decision failed locally: one deep uncapped truncation pile-up (VIM) switched the
rules off for a whole chunk strand, and small cell clusters had too few reads to decide.

The fix being built for LRAA v0.47.0 decides once per **library**, before any chunking, from
the distribution of capped fractions over all TSS peaks. This report shows that distribution
for fourteen libraries, the decision the pre-pass makes from it, and how the FTD sites we know to
be false look on it.

Tables: `Makefile` here, running LRAA's own pre-pass module (`pylib/TSS_cap_calibration.py`),
so peaks, read rules and the decision are exactly LRAA's.

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 11, dpi = 120)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(tidyverse); library(data.table); library(jsonlite) })
pct = function(x, d = 1) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x))
libs = tribble(~lib, ~label, ~platform,
  "FTD", "FTD cortex nuclei", "sc Kinnex 10x 3'",
  "PBMC", "PBMCs", "sc Kinnex 10x 3'",
  "BT474", "BT474", "bulk PacBio",
  "K562", "K562", "bulk PacBio",
  "HG002", "HG002", "bulk PacBio",
  "UHRR", "UHRR", "bulk PacBio",
  "MCF7", "MCF7", "bulk ONT PCS109",
  "A549", "A549", "bulk ONT PCS109",
  "MORF_PB", "MORFs (PacBio)", "trimmed, no cap",
  "MORF_ONT", "MORFs (ONT)", "trimmed, no cap",
  "SIRV", "SIRV spike-ins (BT474 lib.)", "uncapped",
  "SIRV_HG002", "SIRV spike-ins (HG002 lib.)", "uncapped",
  "SIRV_UHRR", "SIRV spike-ins (UHRR lib.)", "uncapped",
  "ARA", "Arabidopsis simulation", "simulated")
libs$label = factor(libs$label, levels = libs$label)
cal = map_dfr(libs$lib, function(l) {
  j = fromJSON(sprintf("out/%s.TSS_cap_calibration.json", l))$stats
  g = function(k) if (is.null(j[[k]])) NA else j[[k]]
  tibble(lib = l, decision = g("decision"), baseline = g("baseline_G_run"), peaks_judged = g("peaks_judged"),
         min_reads = g("peak_min_informative_reads"), uncapped_median = g("uncapped_mode_median"),
         capped_median = g("capped_mode_median"), capped_mode_frac = g("capped_mode_frac"),
         capped_mode_peaks = g("capped_mode_peaks"), separation = g("mode_separation"),
         split = g("mode_split"), valley = g("valley"), off_peak = g("capped_off_peak"),
         per_site = g("per_site_threshold"), reason = g("reason"))
}) %>% left_join(libs, by = "lib")
peaks = map_dfr(libs$lib, ~ fread(sprintf("out/%s.peaks.tsv.gz", .x))[, lib := .x]) %>% left_join(libs, by = "lib")
MIN = cal$min_reads[1]
judged = peaks %>% filter(n_informative >= MIN)
human = c("FTD", "PBMC", "BT474", "K562", "HG002", "UHRR", "MCF7", "A549")
```

## Definitions

- **Read start.** A primary alignment's 5' end on its transcribed strand (minimap2 `ts` tag,
  LRAA's `transcribed_strand`). It counts only if its 5' soft clip is accounted for, as in LRAA's
  `Pretty_alignment`: the clip is nothing but 1-3 G's, or ends in a run of at least 3 G's next
  to the alignment (ONT: adapter + primer + G run).
- **G run.** The run of G's in that clip touching the alignment, recorded before LRAA strips it.
- **Informative.** A read whose genomic base just 5' of its start is not G (otherwise a capped
  read's extra G aligns and the read shows nothing). Only spliced informative reads enter the
  statistics: unspliced reads pile up at nuclear truncation points.
- **Baseline and capped.** The baseline is the most common G run among informative starts away
  from every peak (0 for sc Kinnex, 1 for bulk PacBio, 3 for ONT PCS109, whose primer carries
  GGG). A read is *capped* when its G run exceeds the baseline.
- **Peak.** A TSS candidate called as an LRAA graph build calls one: at least 5 read starts
  pooled within 50 nt (`aggregate_sites_within_window`), at least 5x the median of its non-zero
  neighbours within 50 nt (`filter_non_peaky_positions`). A peak's reads are the informative
  spliced starts within 50 nt of it. Peaks with at least `r MIN` such reads are judged.

## The baseline G run: evidence per library

The baseline is not set by platform: each library's calibration measures it, as the most
common G run among informative spliced read starts away from every peak. Two pieces of evidence
that the measured value is right:

```{r baseline_offpeak}
offp = map_dfr(libs$lib, function(l) {
  h = fromJSON(sprintf("out/%s.TSS_cap_calibration.json", l))$stats$G_run_off_peak
  tibble(lib = l, G = as.integer(names(h)), n = unlist(h))
}) %>% group_by(lib) %>% mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>% left_join(libs, by = "lib")
offp %>% filter(G <= 5) %>% mutate(cell = pct(share)) %>% select(label, platform, G, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = G, values_from = cell, names_prefix = "G run ", values_fill = "") %>%
  left_join(cal %>% transmute(label, baseline = baseline), by = "label") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "1. Off-peak informative spliced starts by 5' G run (share); the most common is the baseline")
sh = function(l, g) { x = offp %>% filter(lib == l, G == g) %>% pull(share); if (length(x)) x else 0 }
```

**1. The off-peak distribution has one clear mode.** It is G run 0 for the sc Kinnex libraries
(`r pct(sh("FTD", 0))` and `r pct(sh("PBMC", 0))` of off-peak starts), 1 for bulk PacBio
(`r pct(sh("BT474", 1))`, `r pct(sh("K562", 1))`, `r pct(sh("HG002", 1))`, `r pct(sh("UHRR", 1))`
for BT474, K562, HG002, UHRR) and 3 for ONT PCS109 (`r pct(sh("MCF7", 3))`,
`r pct(sh("A549", 3))`). The next value up (1, 2 and 4 respectively) is the second most common
because the off-peak pool also holds capped starts that were not called peaks (section 4).
The SIRV spike-ins are an internal control: uncapped RNAs sequenced in the same bulk PacBio
libraries. Their off-peak starts carry exactly one G in `r pct(sh("SIRV", 1))`,
`r pct(sh("SIRV_HG002", 1))` and `r pct(sh("SIRV_UHRR", 1))` of reads (BT474, HG002, UHRR
libraries), two in only `r pct(sh("SIRV", 2))`-`r pct(sh("SIRV_UHRR", 2))`; at their peaks (the spike-ins' real, uncapped 5' ends, figure below)
reads carry zero or one G and almost never two. In BT474's own capped-mode peaks most reads
carry two. So in this chemistry an uncapped end shows at most one G and the cap adds the second:
the baseline of 1 is the library's background, not an artefact of capped reads in the pool. The
likely source of that background G is an extra G in the bulk Kinnex PCR adapters (B. Haas,
2026-10-29). The spike-ins carry it too, and the uncapped 5' ends show it on about half their
reads, so it may not survive adapter trimming on every read. The calibration does not depend on
the cause: it measures the baseline from each library's own reads.

**2. Uncapped-mode peaks sit at the baseline; capped-mode peaks carry one G more.** The reads of
the judged peaks, pooled by mode (split at each library's *t*), by G run:

```{r baseline_modes, fig.height = 8}
gcols = paste0("G", 0:8)
prof = judged %>% left_join(cal %>% select(lib, split), by = "lib") %>%
  mutate(mode = case_when(is.na(split) ~ "all judged peaks", capped_frac < split ~ "uncapped mode", TRUE ~ "capped mode")) %>%
  select(lib, label, mode, all_of(gcols)) %>% pivot_longer(all_of(gcols), names_to = "G", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(G = as.integer(sub("G", "", G))) %>% group_by(lib, label, mode, G) %>% summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(lib, label, mode) %>% mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>% filter(G <= 6)
bl = cal %>% select(label, baseline) %>% filter(!is.na(baseline))
ggplot(prof, aes(G, share, fill = mode)) + geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.75) +
  geom_vline(data = bl, aes(xintercept = baseline), linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("uncapped mode" = "grey55", "capped mode" = "darkorange", "all judged peaks" = "steelblue")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) + facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 5) +
  labs(x = "5' G run of the read (dotted: the library's measured baseline)", y = "share of the peaks' informative reads", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r baseline_modes_table}
prof %>% left_join(cal %>% select(lib, baseline), by = "lib") %>%
  filter(mode != "all judged peaks", G == baseline | G == baseline + 1) %>%
  mutate(which = if_else(G == baseline, "at baseline", "baseline + 1"), cell = pct(share)) %>%
  select(label, mode, which, cell) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = c(mode, which), values_from = cell) %>%
  arrange(label) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("2. Share of the peaks' reads at the baseline G run and one above it, by mode",
                               "(for the MORFs, the SIRVs and the simulation the 'capped mode' is only their sparse tail; the decision is off)"))
```

In every library with the signature, the reads of uncapped-mode peaks are mostly at the baseline
(the truncation products carry only the library's background G's), and the capped-mode peaks gain
reads at exactly baseline + 1 (the extra G opposite the cap): 0 to 1 for sc Kinnex, 1 to 2 for
bulk PacBio, 3 to 4 for ONT. Runs two or more above the baseline stay rare in both modes, so the
signature is one G, not a general lengthening. In the libraries without the signature nearly
all reads sit at the baseline; their few capped-looking peaks are the sparse tail the share
floor rejects. This is the same one-G-over-baseline pattern measured at annotated
TSSs against transcript bodies in `../cap_signature_other_datasets/`.

The same data as enrichment: for each G run, the share of capped-mode reads with that run over
the share of uncapped-mode reads with it (log2; 0 = the two modes alike). Libraries whose
decision is on only: without the signature the "capped mode" is by construction the few peaks
that happen to carry stray G's, set against an uncapped share near zero, so the ratio is large
and meaningless there. G runs with fewer than 20 reads in either mode are left out.

```{r baseline_enrichment, fig.height = 8}
enr = prof %>% filter(mode != "all judged peaks") %>% select(lib, label, mode, G, n, share) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = mode, values_from = c(n, share), values_fill = 0) %>%
  filter(`n_capped mode` >= 20, `n_uncapped mode` >= 20) %>%
  mutate(log2_enrichment = log2(`share_capped mode` / `share_uncapped mode`)) %>%
  left_join(cal %>% select(lib, baseline, decision), by = "lib") %>% filter(decision == "on") %>%
  mutate(rel = case_when(G == baseline ~ "baseline", G == baseline + 1 ~ "baseline + 1", TRUE ~ "other"))
ggplot(enr, aes(G, log2_enrichment, fill = rel)) + geom_col(width = 0.75) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("baseline" = "grey55", "baseline + 1" = "darkorange", "other" = "grey80")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) + facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = "5' G run of the read", y = "log2(capped-mode share / uncapped-mode share)",
       fill = "G run relative to the library's measured baseline") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r baseline_enrichment_table}
top = enr %>% group_by(label) %>% slice_max(log2_enrichment, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(label, top_G = G)
enr %>% filter(rel == "baseline + 1") %>% left_join(top, by = "label") %>%
  transmute(library = label, decision, baseline, `baseline + 1` = G,
            `capped / uncapped share` = sprintf("%.1fx", 2^log2_enrichment),
            `most enriched G run` = top_G) %>% arrange(library) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Enrichment at baseline + 1, and the most enriched G run")
```

In every library with the signature, baseline + 1 is the most enriched G run
(`r sprintf("%.0f", min(2^enr$log2_enrichment[enr$rel == "baseline + 1"]))`- to
`r sprintf("%.0f", max(2^enr$log2_enrichment[enr$rel == "baseline + 1"]))`-fold: the cap's extra
G), and the baseline itself is depleted. The next run up (baseline + 2) is enriched too, less
strongly: some capped molecules carry two extra G's, as when reverse transcriptase adds two C's
at the cap. Such reads are few (they barely show in the share plot above), which is why
"capped" is defined as any run above the baseline rather than exactly one above it.


## How the calibration works: algorithm and code walkthrough

All of it lives in one LRAA module, `pylib/TSS_cap_calibration.py`. The steps, with the
function that does each:

```
calibrate(bam, genome)                     # LRAA driver, or util/calibrate_TSS_cap_signature.py
 ├─ scan(bam, genome, cpu)                 # one worker per contig (largest first), in parallel
 │   └─ scan_contig(bam, genome, contig)   # both strands of one contig, one pass over its reads
 │       ├─ for each primary read:         #   transcribed strand (Util_funcs.transcribed_strand)
 │       │     _five_prime_start(read)     #   -> (5' position, G run or None, spliced?) or None
 │       │       └─ five_prime_clip(clip)  #   the 5' soft-clip rule (same as Pretty_alignment)
 │       ├─ peaks = LRAA's own TSS peak calling on all read starts of the strand
 │       └─ returns, per strand: off-peak G-run counts, and G-run counts at each peak
 ├─ decide(per_contig)                     # pools every contig strand -> one library answer
 │   ├─ baseline   = most common G run among off-peak starts
 │   ├─ fractions  = per peak: capped / informative (peaks with >= 20 informative reads)
 │   ├─ split      = _split_two_modes(fractions)          # Otsu threshold
 │   └─ decision   = on / off / undetermined (criteria below)
 ├─ overrides_from(...)                    # -> LRAA config keys
 └─ write_report / write_scan_table        # .json, .hist.tsv, .svg, .scan.tsv.gz
```

### Step 1: what one read contributes (`_five_prime_start`, `five_prime_clip`)

For each primary alignment (mapping quality at least LRAA's `min_mapping_quality`):

1. Its **transcribed strand** sets which end is 5': the left end on +, the right end on -.
2. Its **5' soft clip** is read in the genomic frame (on - the 5' G run appears as C's at the
   head of the right clip). The **G run** is the run of G's touching the alignment.
3. The read's **5' end is trusted** -- taken as the first base of the molecule it came from --
   only if the clip is accounted for, the rule `Pretty_alignment` applies before assembly: the
   clip is nothing but 1-3 G's, or the G run next to the alignment is at least 3 (ONT: adapter +
   primer + G run). Anything else (a clip with unexplained bases) means the true 5' end is not
   known, and the read is skipped. A trusted 5' end is a real molecule end, not necessarily a
   TSS: most trusted ends away from peaks are truncated or degraded molecules, which is why the
   off-peak ones measure the uncapped baseline.
4. It is **informative** only if the genomic base just upstream of the start is not G.
   Otherwise a capped read's extra G matches the genome, aligns, and no clip is left to see.
5. Only **spliced** reads enter the cap statistics (unspliced reads pile up at nuclear
   truncation points); all accepted starts, spliced or not, are used to call peaks.

Two different questions are asked of every read, and the libraries answer them differently
because their reads arrive in different shapes. LRAA applies the same rules to every library
and does not know the platform.

- **Can the start be trusted?** (step 3) A clip of unexplained bases means the read may be
  misaligned or truncated, so its start is not a transcript 5' end. The clip must be accounted
  for. Kinnex and Iso-Seq reads arrive with the template-switch oligo already trimmed, so at
  most the untemplated G's remain: the clip must be nothing but 1-3 G's. ONT PCS109 reads still
  carry adapter + the strand-switching primer, whose 3' end is **GGG** (it anneals to the C's
  reverse transcriptase adds at the RNA's end). So **>= 3 G's next to the alignment does not mean
  capped**: it means the clip ends in the primer, the base after it is the true first base of
  the cDNA, and the rest of the clip is adapter. Every strand-switched ONT read has those three
  G's, capped or not.
- **Is the read capped?** Decided against the library's baseline, the G count of its uncapped
  starts: 0 for Kinnex, 1 for bulk PacBio (likely an extra G in the bulk Kinnex PCR adapters), 3 for ONT (the primer's
  GGG). A capped end carries **one G more** than the baseline, from the C reverse transcriptase
  adds opposite the cap.

Examples (+ strand reads, LRAA defaults), each in the library type that produces it:

| library (baseline) | 5' clip | G run | start trusted? | capped? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sc Kinnex (0) | (none) | 0 | yes | no |
| sc Kinnex (0) | `G` | 1 | yes: the clip is all G | **yes** (1 > 0) |
| sc Kinnex (0) | `GG` | 2 | yes: the clip is all G | **yes** |
| sc Kinnex (0) | `A` | 0 | no: an unexplained base | (not counted) |
| sc Kinnex (0) | `AG` | 1 | no: not all G, and fewer than 3 G's | (not counted) |
| bulk PacBio (1) | `G` | 1 | yes | no (1 = baseline) |
| bulk PacBio (1) | `GG` | 2 | yes | **yes** (2 > 1) |
| ONT PCS109 (3) | adapter + `...GGG` | 3 | yes: the clip ends in the primer | no (3 = baseline) |
| ONT PCS109 (3) | adapter + `...GGGG` | 4 | yes | **yes** (4 > 3) |
| ONT PCS109 (3) | adapter + `...GG` | 2 | no: the clip does not end in the primer | (not counted) |

An uncapped ONT end can still show a 4th G when only two of the primer's G's anneal to the
three C's, leaving one C to template an extra G. That is why ONT's uncapped mode sits higher
(section 1) and its two modes are closer together.

`pylib/test_TSS_cap_calibration.py` checks that `five_prime_clip` gives the same G run and the
same verdict as `Pretty_alignment` for these clips, on both strands.

### Step 2: peaks and per-peak counts (`scan_contig`)

Per contig strand, all accepted read starts go into a position counter, and peaks are called
exactly as a splice-graph build calls TSS candidates:

- `aggregate_sites_within_window`: positions with at least 5 starts pooled within 50 nt,
  keeping the strongest position of each cluster;
- `filter_non_peaky_positions`: a peak must have at least 5x the median count of its non-zero
  neighbours within 50 nt (a sharp pile-up, not a smear).

Each informative spliced start within 50 nt of a peak is counted for that peak by its G run
(`G0`..`G8`); every other informative spliced start goes to the strand's **off-peak** counts.
A worker returns only these counts, so the parent can pool contigs without the reads.

### Step 3: the library decision (`decide`, `_split_two_modes`)

```
baseline   = argmax_g  off_peak_count[g]            # e.g. 0 Kinnex, 1 PacBio, 3 ONT
for each peak with n = informative reads >= 20:
    capped_frac = (reads with G run > baseline) / n
if number of such peaks < 50:            -> undetermined   ("too few peaks to judge")

t = Otsu threshold over capped_frac      # the cut t in 0.01..0.99 maximising
                                         #   w_lo * w_hi * (mean_hi - mean_lo)^2
lo = peaks with capped_frac <  t         # uncapped group
hi = peaks with capped_frac >= t         # capped group
share = |hi| / (|lo| + |hi|)
sep   = median(hi) - median(lo)

if share >= 0.10 and |hi| >= 50 and sep >= 0.20:   -> on
elif share >= 0.10 and sep >= 0.20:                 -> undetermined   (clear but thin: |hi| < 50)
else:                                               -> off
```

In the Otsu criterion, for a candidate threshold *t*:

- **w_lo** is the fraction of judged peaks with capped fraction below *t*, and **mean_lo** their
  mean capped fraction (the uncapped group);
- **w_hi** = 1 - w_lo is the fraction at or above *t*, and **mean_hi** their mean (the capped
  group).

w_lo * w_hi * (mean_hi - mean_lo)^2 is the between-group variance written compactly. In full it
is w_lo * (mean_lo - mu)^2 + w_hi * (mean_hi - mu)^2, each group's weight times the squared
distance of its mean from the overall mean mu = w_lo * mean_lo + w_hi * mean_hi; substituting mu
gives the compact form. The total variance of the peaks is fixed and equals this between-group
part plus the within-group spread, so the *t* that maximises it is also the one leaving the two
groups tightest, which is the valley of a bimodal histogram. The weights stop a cut that isolates
a handful of extreme peaks from scoring well: w_lo * w_hi is largest for an even split and goes
to 0 as either group empties.

The **valley** reported alongside is the emptiest 2% histogram bin between the two medians;
it is not used in the decision.

`overrides_from` turns the answer into LRAA config keys: "on" or "off" sets
`TSS_cap_signature` and `TSS_cap_G_baseline`, so every splice-graph build applies the
library's answer and estimates nothing; "undetermined" sets nothing, and each graph build
decides from its own reads as before (`TSS_cap_signature` "auto").

### Worked example: FTD

```{r otsu_ftd, fig.height = 3.6}
f = sort(judged$capped_frac[judged$lib == "FTD"])
otsu = tibble(t = (1:99) / 100) %>% rowwise() %>% mutate(
  w_lo = mean(f < t), w_hi = 1 - w_lo,
  m_lo = if (w_lo > 0) mean(f[f < t]) else NA, m_hi = if (w_hi > 0) mean(f[f >= t]) else NA,
  between_var = w_lo * w_hi * (m_hi - m_lo)^2) %>% ungroup()
ftd = cal %>% filter(lib == "FTD")
p1 = ggplot(judged %>% filter(lib == "FTD"), aes(capped_frac)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "grey45") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ftd$split, colour = "darkgreen") + scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "capped fraction", y = "peaks (log)", title = "FTD peaks and the Otsu split") + theme_bw()
p2 = ggplot(otsu, aes(t, between_var)) + geom_line() + geom_vline(xintercept = ftd$split, colour = "darkgreen") +
  labs(x = "candidate threshold t", y = "between-group variance", title = "Otsu: pick the t that maximises it") + theme_bw()
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(patchwork)); p1 + p2
n_all = sum(peaks$lib == "FTD")
```

For FTD (`r n_all` peaks called genome-wide):

1. **Baseline**: off-peak starts are mostly G run 0, so baseline = `r ftd$baseline`; a read
   with one or more untemplated G's counts as capped.
2. **Judged peaks**: `r ftd$peaks_judged` peaks have at least `r MIN` informative spliced reads.
3. **Split**: the between-group variance peaks at t = `r ftd$split` (right panel). The curve
   is nearly flat from about 0.1 to 0.35: so few peaks sit in the valley that any cut there
   gives almost the same two groups, which is why the decision does not hinge on exactly
   where the cut falls. Below it,
   `r ftd$peaks_judged - ftd$capped_mode_peaks` peaks with median capped fraction
   `r pct(ftd$uncapped_median)`; above it, `r ftd$capped_mode_peaks` peaks with median
   `r pct(ftd$capped_median)`.
4. **Criteria**: capped share `r pct(ftd$capped_mode_frac)` (needs >= 10%), capped-group peaks
   `r ftd$capped_mode_peaks` (needs >= 50), separation `r round(ftd$separation, 2)`
   (needs >= 0.20): all pass, so the decision is **`r ftd$decision`**, and every graph build gets
   `TSS_cap_signature` "on" with `TSS_cap_G_baseline` `r ftd$baseline`.

For the libraries without the signature, the split still finds a "capped" group (Otsu always
splits), but it is a sparse tail of peaks with a few stray G's, so the share criterion fails:
the Arabidopsis simulation's capped group is
`r pct(cal$capped_mode_frac[cal$lib == "ARA"])` of its peaks
(`r cal$capped_mode_peaks[cal$lib == "ARA"]` peaks; t = `r cal$split[cal$lib == "ARA"]`), the
MORFs' `r pct(cal$capped_mode_frac[cal$lib == "MORF_PB"])` (PacBio) and
`r pct(cal$capped_mode_frac[cal$lib == "MORF_ONT"])` (ONT): **off**. Their medians are far
enough apart (separation `r round(cal$separation[cal$lib == "ARA"], 2)` for the simulation),
so the share floor is what rejects them. The SIRVs of the BT474 library give only
`r cal$peaks_judged[cal$lib == "SIRV"]` judged peaks: **undetermined**; those of the HG002 and
UHRR libraries give `r cal$peaks_judged[cal$lib == "SIRV_HG002"]` and
`r cal$peaks_judged[cal$lib == "SIRV_UHRR"]`, with modes only
`r round(cal$separation[cal$lib == "SIRV_HG002"], 2)` and
`r round(cal$separation[cal$lib == "SIRV_UHRR"], 2)` apart: **off**.

The split *t* itself is not tested: it always lies between the two group medians, so with
medians at least 0.20 apart it sits well above the uncapped mode. Measured, *t* is
`r min(cal$split[cal$decision == "on"])`-`r max(cal$split[cal$decision == "on"])` where the
decision is on, and `r min(cal$split[cal$decision == "off"], na.rm = TRUE)`-`r max(cal$split[cal$decision == "off"], na.rm = TRUE)`
where it is off.

### After the decision: the per-site rules

The calibration only says whether the signature exists and what the baseline is. The rules that
remove sites are unchanged, and use it per site (a site's informative reads within 50 nt):

- **Pooled / basic runs** (`prune_uncapped_alt_TSS`): a TSS downstream of a capped TSS, on any
  splice-graph path, is pruned when it has at least 5 informative reads and under 10% capped.
  A gene's upstream-most TSS is never judged.
- **Cluster runs** (`require_cap_for_new_TSS`, set by the single-cell workflow): a TSS not within
  50 nt of a guide 5' end needs at least 5 informative reads, at least 2 capped, and at least 10%
  capped.

### Where it runs

- **LRAA**: at the start of a discovery run with `TSS_cap_signature` "auto" (in chunked mode
  after the library read count); the answer reaches every chunk worker with the forwarded config.
  Quant-only runs skip it.
- **Standalone**: `util/calibrate_TSS_cap_signature.py --bam --genome --output_prefix`, or
  `--scan_table` to re-decide from a saved scan; it writes a `.config.json` for LRAA's
  `--config_update`, with `TSS_cap_prepass` false so no later run re-calibrates on its own reads.
- **WDL**: `LRAA.wdl` runs the standalone step once on the whole bam before sharding and merges
  the answer into every shard's config; `LRAA-singlecell.wdl` hands the init run's answer to every
  cluster run, so a cluster never decides from its own sparse reads.

## 1. Per-peak capped fractions are bimodal when the library has the signature

```{r hist_all, fig.height = 15}
lines = cal %>% select(label, split, valley, per_site) %>% pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "line", values_to = "x") %>%
  filter(!is.na(x)) %>%
  mutate(line = recode(line, split = "Otsu split t", valley = "valley", per_site = "per-site threshold (10%)"))
f3 = function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "-", sprintf("%.2f", x))
ann = cal %>% transmute(label, txt = ifelse(is.na(split),
    sprintf("%s\n%s judged peaks\n%s", decision, peaks_judged, replace_na(reason, "")),
    sprintf("%s\nt = %s\ncapped share %s (%s peaks)\nmedians %s / %s, sep %s",
            decision, f3(split), pct(capped_mode_frac, 0), capped_mode_peaks,
            pct(uncapped_median), pct(capped_median), f3(separation))))
ggplot(judged, aes(capped_frac)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "grey45") +
  geom_vline(data = lines, aes(xintercept = x, linetype = line, colour = line)) +
  geom_label(data = ann, aes(x = 1, y = Inf, label = txt), hjust = 1, vjust = 1.05, size = 2.6,
             label.size = 0, fill = alpha("white", 0.85), inherit.aes = FALSE, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Otsu split t" = "darkgreen", "valley" = "steelblue", "per-site threshold (10%)" = "red3")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Otsu split t" = "solid", "valley" = "dotted", "per-site threshold (10%)" = "dashed")) +
  scale_y_log10(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.6))) + facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "capped fraction of a peak's informative spliced read starts", y = "TSS peaks (log scale)",
       colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       title = sprintf("Peaks with >= %d informative spliced reads; label: the decision and the values it rests on", MIN),
       subtitle = "on: capped share >= 10%, >= 50 capped-group peaks, medians >= 0.20 apart") +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r cal_table}
cal %>% transmute(library = label, platform, decision, `baseline G` = baseline, `peaks judged` = peaks_judged,
                  `uncapped mode median` = pct(uncapped_median), `capped mode median` = pct(capped_median),
                  `capped mode share` = pct(capped_mode_frac), separation = round(separation, 2),
                  valley = valley, reason = replace_na(reason, "")) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "LRAA's library decision (TSS_cap_calibration.decide)")
```

Every library made with template switching has two modes: peaks whose reads are almost never
capped (uncapped-mode medians `r pct(min(cal$uncapped_median[cal$lib %in% human]))` to
`r pct(max(cal$uncapped_median[cal$lib %in% human]))`), and peaks whose reads mostly are
(capped-mode medians `r pct(min(cal$capped_median[cal$lib %in% human]))` to
`r pct(max(cal$capped_median[cal$lib %in% human]))`). The libraries without the signature have
one mode at zero. The ONT libraries' modes are broader and closer together, and their uncapped
mode sits higher (`r pct(cal$uncapped_median[cal$lib == "MCF7"])` and
`r pct(cal$uncapped_median[cal$lib == "A549"])`): an uncapped end can still carry a fourth G
when only two of the primer's G's anneal.

**The decision.** The fractions are split into two groups where they separate best (Otsu). The
signature is present when the capped group holds at least 10% of the judged peaks and at least
50 peaks, and its median exceeds the uncapped group's by at least 0.20. With fewer than 50
judged peaks, or a clear but thin capped mode, the result is *undetermined*: nothing is set, and
each graph build decides for itself as before. The MORF reads (5' ends trimmed upstream) show a
sparse tail of capped-looking peaks (`r pct(cal$capped_mode_frac[cal$lib == "MORF_PB"])` of
peaks) that the 10% floor rejects.

**The valley** (emptiest 2% bin between the two medians) lies at or above the per-site threshold
LRAA uses (`min_TSS_cap_frac` 10%) in every library with the signature, so the per-site rule
cuts inside the uncapped mode's upper tail or at the valley, never into the capped mode.

## 2. The capped mode is the CAGE-supported one

```{r cage_hist, fig.height = 8}
hj = judged %>% filter(lib %in% human) %>% mutate(CAGE = if_else(in_CAGE, "at a FANTOM5 CAGE peak (+-25 nt)", "no CAGE peak"))
ggplot(hj, aes(capped_frac, fill = CAGE)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, position = "identity", alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "capped fraction", y = "TSS peaks", fill = NULL) + theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r cage_table}
bands = c(0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1.0001)
cage_tab = hj %>% mutate(band = cut(capped_frac, bands, right = FALSE,
                                     labels = c("0-5%", "5-10%", "10-20%", ">=20%"))) %>%
  group_by(label, band) %>% summarise(peaks = n(), in_CAGE = mean(in_CAGE), .groups = "drop")
cage_tab %>% mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%s)", peaks, pct(in_CAGE, 0))) %>% select(label, band, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = band, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Peaks per capped-fraction band (share at a CAGE peak)")
cg = function(l, b) cage_tab %>% filter(label == l, band == b) %>% pull(in_CAGE)
lo_ftd = hj %>% filter(lib == "FTD", capped_frac < 0.05)
```

In FTD, `r pct(cg("FTD cortex nuclei", ">=20%"), 0)` of capped-mode peaks (>= 20%) sit at a
CAGE peak, against `r pct(cg("FTD cortex nuclei", "0-5%"), 0)` of uncapped-mode peaks (< 5%);
in PBMCs `r pct(cg("PBMCs", ">=20%"), 0)` against `r pct(cg("PBMCs", "0-5%"), 0)`. The
uncapped-mode peaks that do overlap CAGE (`r sum(lo_ftd$in_CAGE)` in FTD) are probably FANTOM5's
exon-internal peaks, common at recapping and cleavage sites: VIM's downstream site is one
(0 capped of 108 informative reads, on a CAGE peak). The PBMC capped mode includes non-CAGE
peaks (`r pct(1 - cg("PBMCs", ">=20%"), 0)`): capped starts FANTOM5 lacks, which the cap rule
keeps.

## 3. Sites known to be false sit with the transcript body

The FTD event pairs (`ext/`, the v0.45.0 high-confidence TSS switches where a neuron cluster
favours the downstream site, before any cap rule): the downstream sites are 5' truncation
products by every other measure (no CAGE support, neuron nuclei's short reads; see
`../../LRAA_paper-FTD_study/__Site_Usage_Analysis`). Their capped fractions, from the same
read rules:

```{r event_sites, fig.height = 4.5}
ev = fread("out/FTD.event_site_caprates.tsv")[n_informative_spliced >= 20][, frac := n_capped_spliced / n_informative_spliced]
body = map_dfr(c(FTD = "../ALS.capsig.tsv.gz", PBMC = "../PBMC.capsig.tsv.gz"), function(f) {
  fread(f)[upstream_G == 0, .(reads = sum(reads)), by = .(five_class, clip)][, .(G_share = sum(reads[clip == "G"]) / sum(reads)), by = five_class]
}, .id = "dataset")
ev_s = ev[, .(sites = .N, median = median(frac), q25 = quantile(frac, .25), q75 = quantile(frac, .75),
              le3 = sum(frac <= 0.03), ge10 = sum(frac >= 0.10)), by = role]
U = ev_s[role == "U"]; Dn = ev_s[role == "D"]
ftd_modes = cal %>% filter(lib == "FTD")
ggplot(ev, aes(frac, fill = role)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, alpha = .7, position = "identity") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = body$G_share[body$dataset == "FTD" & body$five_class == "body"], linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(U = "steelblue", D = "darkorange"), labels = c(U = "upstream site (real)", D = "downstream site (false)")) +
  labs(x = "capped fraction of informative spliced starts (dotted: FTD transcript-body rate)", y = "sites", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

| | sites | median capped | middle half | sites <= 3% | sites >= 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| upstream (real) sites | `r U$sites` | `r pct(U$median)` | `r pct(U$q25)`-`r pct(U$q75)` | `r U$le3` | `r U$ge10` |
| downstream (false) sites | `r Dn$sites` | `r pct(Dn$median)` | `r pct(Dn$q25)`-`r pct(Dn$q75)` | `r Dn$le3` | `r Dn$ge10` |
| FTD transcript body | | `r pct(body$G_share[body$dataset == "FTD" & body$five_class == "body"], 2)` | | | |
| FTD library: uncapped / capped mode median | | `r pct(ftd_modes$uncapped_median)` / `r pct(ftd_modes$capped_median)` | | | |

The false downstream sites have the transcript body's cap rate and sit in the library's
uncapped mode; their real upstream partners sit in the capped mode. The `r Dn$ge10` downstream
sites at >= 10% are candidates for genuine alternative promoters, which the cap rule keeps.
The body rates come from the 5' completeness tables (`../`; reads starting > 100 nt inside
single-TSS genes): FTD `r pct(body$G_share[body$dataset == "FTD" & body$five_class == "body"], 2)`,
PBMC `r pct(body$G_share[body$dataset == "PBMC" & body$five_class == "body"], 2)`.

## 4. Why the decision does not use a non-peak background

v0.46.x compared peaks against read starts away from every peak. That "background" is not
uncapped: it holds real capped starts that were not called peaks.

```{r strata}
st = map_dfr(c(FTD = "out/FTD.chr19.offpeak_strata.tsv", PBMC = "out/PBMC.chr19.offpeak_strata.tsv",
               BT474 = "out/BT474.chr19.offpeak_strata.tsv"), fread, .id = "library") %>%
  mutate(capped = n_capped / n_informative)
st %>% mutate(cell = sprintf("%s (%d)", pct(capped), n_informative)) %>%
  select(library, distance_to_peak, reads_starting_at_position, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = library, values_from = cell) %>%
  arrange(factor(distance_to_peak, levels = unique(c("at peak (<=50 nt)", "51-200 nt", "201-1000 nt", "1001-5000 nt", "5001-inf nt"))), reads_starting_at_position) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "chr19: capped share of informative spliced starts (n reads), by distance to the nearest peak and by how many reads start at the same position")
```

Starts just outside a peak's 50 nt window are often capped (promoters spread their starts),
and so are positions far from any peak where several reads start (real promoters the peak
filter missed: broad, or lowly expressed). Even single starts far from any peak run above the
transcript-body rate. The per-peak distribution needs no such background: the uncapped mode
*is* the truncation background, measured where it matters.

## 5. Sensitivity to the read floor for judged peaks

```{r floors}
fl = map_dfr(c(10, 20, 50), function(m) peaks %>% filter(n_informative >= m) %>% group_by(label) %>%
  summarise(floor = m, peaks = n(), `< 10%` = mean(capped_frac < .10), `10-20%` = mean(capped_frac >= .10 & capped_frac < .20),
            `>= 20%` = mean(capped_frac >= .20), .groups = "drop"))
fl %>% filter(label %in% libs$label[libs$lib %in% c(human, "MORF_PB")]) %>%
  mutate(across(c(`< 10%`, `10-20%`, `>= 20%`), ~ pct(.x))) %>% arrange(label, floor) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Share of peaks per band at three read floors")
```

The between-mode band stays thin at every floor; a lower floor adds binomial noise to both modes,
a higher one drops the lowly expressed genes. LRAA uses `r MIN`.

## Possible extension: a fitted mixture model (not pursued now)

Recorded 2026-10-29 for later; the threshold rule above is kept for its simplicity. The
per-peak counts (informative reads *n*, capped reads *k*) could be fitted with a
two-component **beta-binomial mixture** (EM): the binomial part weighs each peak by its depth,
the beta part allows real spread within a mode. It would give

- a model-based library decision in place of the Otsu split: two components preferred over
  one (BIC) *and* effect-size criteria on the fitted parameters (capped weight >= 10%, means
  >= 0.20 apart, separation such as Ashman's D >= 2), since with thousands of peaks BIC alone
  prefers two components for any heterogeneity (the MORF tail would pass);
- per-site posteriors in place of the fixed 10% threshold: a site's probability of belonging
  to the uncapped mode given its *n* and *k*. Thin sites (5 reads, none capped) would no longer
  be pruned on weak evidence, and the cut would adapt per library (the ONT uncapped mode
  reaches past 10%).

First step if taken up: fit the mixture to these fourteen libraries' peak tables and compare its
decisions with the table in section 1. Also recorded in LRAA `docs/TSS_cap_calibration.md`.

## Caveats

- **Mixed bams.** A bam merging libraries of different chemistries has more than one baseline
  (sc Kinnex 0, PacBio bulk 1, ONT 3); one library-wide answer would be wrong for part of it.
  None of our datasets is mixed.
- **The genomic-G blind spot** is unchanged: a site whose genomic base just upstream is G has no
  informative reads and is never judged per site.
- **ONT** keeps more uncapped sites, because its uncapped mode reaches past the 10% per-site
  threshold. A per-library threshold at the valley would fix that; it is reported here
  (`valley`) but not used.
